_note: The tutorials of the game, each shown once on Day 1 of a new save (see scripts/tutorial/tutorial.gd). A phase has one for the whole screen (investigation, monitoring, hardening, response) and some for a view the player opens later (investigation_report, hardening_shop, hardening_deck_editor, hardening_upgrade_editor): a view's tutorial shows the first time the player opens that view. A step is text plus a target: a node path from the scene the tutorial is shown in, or %Name for a node found by name, or empty for a step with nothing to point at. Keep a step to one or two short sentences.

investigation.text: INVESTIGATION. Something went wrong at the office last night. Look through the records and find the clues that show what happened.
Each tab is a different set of records: email, logs, computers, logins, files, network and servers. Check them all.
Click a row to read the whole entry here.
Press INVESTIGATE to look closer. A real clue is marked FOUND. An ordinary entry is only marked READ.
This counts the clues you have found. You need all of them.
With every clue found, a REPORT button appears here. There you say what happened, so take your time.

monitoring.text: MONITORING. You watch the sign-ins as they happen. For each one, decide: normal, or suspicious.
The guide shows the rules: office hours, and who is on call tonight. A sign-in that breaks them is suspicious.
NEXT LOG brings the next sign-in.
Read the log here. Click a part of it to ask about that part.
LET PASS when the sign-in looks normal.
REPORT when it breaks a rule. A wrong call costs you points.
The RULEBOOK has every rule, in case you forget one.
Watch the clock. The shift ends when the time runs out.

hardening.text: HARDENING. Now you prepare. What you set up here decides how the fight goes.
This is your deck: the cards you will play. The panel next to it shows what kinds of cards it holds.
Upgrades are defenses. Every upgrade does two things: ALWAYS is what it gives you in any fight, and AGAINST is what it does to one attack. You must equip it, and each takes some load.
In the shop you spend Security Points on cards and upgrades. You earned them in the last two phases.
Equip the upgrades that answer what you found. The ones marked * match your clues.
Choose which cards are in your deck. You need at least 5.
When you are ready, move on to the fight.

response.text: RESPONSE. The threat attacks. Each round has two parts: you play cards, then you dodge its attack.
Your cards. Hover over one to read it, and click it to play it.
A panel opens beside the card. Its colored words, like Block or Draw, tell you what they mean when you point at them.
Every card costs energy. Your energy is the limit on what you can play each turn.
Above the threat is its next attack, shown before it comes so you can plan. Point at it to read about it.
End your turn to let the threat attack.
Then you steer the heart with the arrow keys or WASD, and dodge the bullets in the box.
The upgrades you equipped show here. Without the right one, that attack comes in a harder version.

response_day3.text: NEW: DODGE. Some cards give Dodge. Each Dodge makes one hit of the enemy turn do nothing, and it is gone when the turn is over.
Your Dodge shows under your HP bar, after Block. Point at it to read it.
The new attacks show their cue in the box: a lock that spreads, a bar that fills, and files from both sides. Watch the box.

investigation_order.text: This time you put what happened in order, from first to last. The times in your notes tell you the order.
Some of the events did happen, but they are not part of the attack. They go in no blank.

recovery_rebuild.text: Put the steps in order, one click after another. A step that comes too early tells you why it has to wait.

recovery_restore.text: Pick a backup from before the red marker, and kept apart from the network. Test it before you restore it.
After the restore, set up the 3-2-1 rule: three copies, on two kinds of storage, one of them offline.

recovery_folders.text: Turn off the access a person does not need, and keep what their job needs. Taking away something they need bounces back.

response_day4.text: NEW: EXPOSED. Some cards Expose the threat. Every card you play after it deals more damage, until the end of your turn.
The threat's Exposed shows under its HP bar. Point at it to read it. Mark the threat first, then hit it.
This threat acts from inside the box: a badge that bursts, a slow copy, and carriers that take files. Stay near a file to guard it.

investigation_know.text: This time you sort what you KNOW from what you do NOT know. The logs show what happened. They never show why.
Put each fact in KNOW and each question in DO NOT KNOW. A guess is not a fact, so it goes in neither.

recovery_account.text: First close the right account. Then choose how to talk to the person. A wrong choice tells you why.

response_day5.text: NEW: CHARGE and LEAK. Charge gives you Energy at the start of your next turn. Leak takes HP at the start of your next turn, and Block cannot stop it.
Both show as small marks under YOUR HP bar. Point at one to read it.
This threat is small and steady, big and homing, and it fires along lanes. Read the strip before each attack.

recovery_archive.text: Two steps. First find the leftover archive and delete it. Then choose who to tell and how. A wrong choice tells you why.

investigation_report.text: THE REPORT. Now you tell what happened. The story has blanks, and you fill them with what you found.
This is the story. Some of its words are missing.
Select a word and drag it into a blank (or use the keyboard). Some of these words do not belong, so choose carefully.
Your notes on the clues you found are here. Use them to decide.
When every blank is filled, submit the report. A wrong word costs you points, so check first.

hardening_shop.text: THE SHOP. Spend your Security Points on cards and upgrades. Click one to read it, then press BUY.
Carla runs the shop. Click anything and she explains it in plain words.
Cards go into your collection. You can buy the same card more than once.
Upgrades are defenses. You can own each one once, so pick the ones that answer what you found.
What you clicked is described here, with its price. Press BUY to pay for it.
Your Security Points are shown here.
Leave when you are done. You can come back before the fight.

hardening_deck_editor.text: THE DECK EDITOR. Choose which cards go into your deck.
This is your deck: 9 cards at most, and at least 5 to start the fight. Click a card to take it out.
Your other cards are here. Click one to put it in the deck. The buttons above filter by type and cost.
Point at any card to read it here.
Need more cards? The shop is one click away.

hardening_upgrade_editor.text: THE UPGRADE EDITOR. Choose the upgrades you will take into the fight.
Each upgrade uses some load, and your load is limited. You cannot equip everything.
Your equipped upgrades are here. Click one to take it off.
Your other upgrades are here. Click one to equip it. A * means it answers a clue you found.
Point at an upgrade to read it. ALWAYS works in every fight. AGAINST stops one attack.

response_day6.text: NEW: CAP. Some cards Cap the enemy's turn: each hit does at most that much damage until the turn is over.
Cap shows as a small mark under YOUR HP bar. Point at it to read it.
This threat floods the box from every side, fires from many sources, and leaves slow connections that stay. Read the strip before each attack.

investigation_compare.text: NEW: two graphs. One is the lunch sale and one is the attack. Look at when each one starts, and what it does after.
Then fill the blanks: which graph is which, when the flood began, and what its requests did and did not do.

recovery_dial.text: Move the dial to set the limit. Blue dots are real customers, red dots are bots. Watch who gets through.

recovery_hardware.text: Hardware jobs go step by step. The next step glows, and a wrong move tells you why.
Always shut a machine down and unplug it before you open it.

response_day7.text: NEW: REFLECT. Some cards Reflect: each time you are hit during the enemy's turn, the threat takes that much damage.
Reflect shows as a small mirror under YOUR HP bar. Point at it to read it.
This threat offers you things. Envelopes carry words: read them before you touch one. Fake ones hurt, real ones heal.

investigation_inspect.text: NEW: two messages. One is real and one is fake, and they look alike. Click a part of a message to look closer.
Then fill the blanks: which message is fake, its sender, where its link really goes, what it asks, and what Ravi did.

recovery_mailbox.text: Three steps. Delete every copy of the fake from the inboxes, build the filter, then choose the warning for the staff.
The real IT notice and the HR message are in the inboxes too. Do not delete those.

response_day8.text: NEW: EXPLOIT. Some cards say Exploit: if the threat is Exposed when you play them, they deal that much more damage. Play an Expose card first.
This threat sends pieces of text. Touch one and the heart holds it: it shows under the box. A quote and a piece of code held together are run, and that hurts.

investigation_query.text: NEW: two queries. Each shows what the website asks its database after someone types something. Press RUN to see the answer.
Then fill the blanks: when it happened, what was typed, where, what the website did, and what was left behind.

recovery_patch.text: Follow the glowing button, one step at a time: back up, download from the maker, check the number, test on the copy, then the live site.
Never try an update on the live site first. A bad update can break it.
